prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: an academic hardware architecture figure for an IEEE-style research paper, wide landscape, white background, flat vector-like line art, restrained navy/teal/gray, thin consistent lines, no gradients, no 3D, no decorative icons, crisp English labels. Draw the exact implemented unified system left-to-right: three vertically stacked boxes 'CPU', 'Vortex SimX', 'CoralNPU RTL' feeding one shared line and box 'Native AXI256', then 'AXI2Flit', then bidirectional 'UCIe', then 'Memory-side dispatcher'. To its right a top branch labeled 'Ordinary accesses' goes directly to a box 'Online mem_sim'. A bottom branch labeled 'MMIO commands' goes to a large dashed rectangle 'SparseGate RTL'; inside that rectangle are boxes 'AXI256 registers', 'FP4 index core', 'Stable Top-K', and 'AXI256 DMA'. DMA connects to the SAME Online mem_sim box, with a clearly labeled bidirectional line 'Index reads / KV gather / result writes'. Show a return arrow underneath through UCIe to the processors labeled 'Read data and completion'. Small understated footer 'One event timeline; one memory image'. Ensure SparseGate is strictly AFTER UCIe, not before. Keep boxes aligned and generous whitespace, no performance numbers, no claim of full LLM, no SRAM macro claim. At paper column scale text should remain readable. Every connection should be unambiguous and labels not overlap arrows.

Use case: scientific-educational. Produce one publication-quality academic block diagram of an implemented digital sparse-index core. Wide landscape 3:2 canvas, strictly opaque solid white background, no transparency, navy outlines with muted teal and light gray fills, black English type, flat vector-like technical illustration, thin arrows, no gradients, no 3D, no icons, no decorative title. Left-top box 'Q buffer' with small second line '32 heads × 128 FP4 values'; left-bottom box 'Shared K buffer' with small second line 'One 128-D vector'. Both feed a central bank clearly containing 16 small parallel cells and the label '16 FP4 lanes'. A single arrow labeled '32-D group sum' leads to 'E8M0 scale alignment', then 'FP32 group accumulation', then 'ReLU', then 'Signed head weight', then 'FP32 head accumulation', then 'Stable min-heap' with second line 'K ≤ 512'. Use two neat rows connected by ONE unambiguous elbow arrow if horizontal space is insufficient: top-row Q/K and FP4 lanes and scale and group accumulation; bottom-row ReLU, weight multiply, head accumulator, heap and final 'Selected indices'. Above the shared K buffer write 'Read once; reuse across heads'. Under the FP4 lane bank write 'Four groups per head'. Draw a small separate input box 'BF16 weights' feeding only Signed head weight. Under the figure include exact subtitle 'Post-projection numeric datapath; digital standard-cell implementation'. All words spelled accurately, no claims of in-SRAM arithmetic, clock rate, area, measured performance, or full-model inference. Show data flowing through arithmetic into heap, not software-provided scores. Legible as an IEEE paper full-width figure.

Use case: scientific-educational. Academic journal hardware figure, opaque pure white background, landscape, crisp English type, navy/teal/gray flat rectangles, no 3D, no gradients, no numbers except exact byte counts. Illustrate THREE precise memory-record layouts as horizontal segmented bars, well separated. Row A label 'Query record: 96 B per head', segments widths proportionally 64,4,2,26, segment labels 'FP4 values: 64 B', 'Scales: 4 B', 'Weight: 2 B', 'Padding: 26 B'. Put small segments' labels as clear callouts above the bars rather than unreadable squeezed text. Row B label 'Index-key record: 96 B', segments 64,4,28, labels 'FP4 values: 64 B', 'Scales: 4 B', 'Padding: 28 B'. Row C label 'Main-KV record: 288 B', segments 256,32, labels 'FP4 values: 256 B', 'Scales: 32 B'. Below A/B, exact annotation 'Indexer: E2M1 + E8M0, group size 32'. Below C exact annotation 'Main KV: E2M1 + E4M3, group size 16'. At bottom show three short small AXI beat boxes aligned across each 96 B row, labeled collectively '3 × 32 B AXI transfers'; for row C note '9 × 32 B AXI transfers'. These illustrate record packaging, not fabricated waveform or performance. No extra fields, no data values, no repeated text, all text must be accurate. Wide blank margins, consistent sans-serif labels. Graphic should be suitable as a serious computer architecture paper figure.

Use case: scientific-educational. Draw a clean academic state-and-dataflow diagram on opaque white background, wide landscape, minimal muted navy/teal/gray, thin rectangular outlines and arrows, no gradients or 3D. Left box 'Host command' feeds a diamond 'Validate context / epoch / addresses'. Its error branch leads downward to 'ERROR; cache invalid'. Its successful branch leads to three clearly separated horizontal lanes. Top lane label 'FULL': 'Read Q' -> 'Read all valid K' -> 'Score + Top-K'. Middle lane label 'REINDEX': 'Read Q + candidate IDs' -> 'Read candidate K only' -> 'Score + Top-K'. Bottom lane label 'REUSE': 'Check committed selection' -> 'Cached indices'; do not show Q or K reads in this lane. All three lanes merge at one right-side box 'Position-ordered indices', then 'Write results + gather KV', then a diamond 'All write responses OK?', then 'DONE; cache committed'. Error response from final diamond goes to the SAME 'ERROR; cache invalid' box via a thin bottom return path. Final footer 'Completion follows real memory responses'. This is exact control behavior, not latency measurement. No performance numbers, no claim that software candidate construction happens in hardware. Legible English labels without overlap, IEEE research-figure style.

prompts.prompt: Edit this existing academic architecture figure. Preserve all boxes, exact labels, their placement, and the SparseGate-after-UCIe topology. Make the background fully opaque solid white; improve thin-line contrast for print. One essential wiring correction: REMOVE the entire long bottom direct return wire from Online mem_sim to the processors. Responses must return along the same main chain, never bypass UCIe. Make every connection in the shared processor -> Native AXI256 -> AXI2Flit -> UCIe -> Memory-side dispatcher -> Online mem_sim path visibly bidirectional using paired arrowheads. Likewise make the dispatcher-to-AXI256-registers connection bidirectional, and keep the AXI256 DMA to Online mem_sim bidirectional. Add a small plain sentence below the chain 'Requests and responses use the same AXI/UCIe path'. Keep the lower SparseGate box with its four internal stages. Preserve the footer 'One event timeline; one memory image'. No invented additional blocks, no numbers, no gradients, no translucent background, no 3D. Crisp academic navy/teal/gray technical figure, white paper.

Edit this existing academic digital-hardware architecture figure. Make ONLY this surgical correction: erase the entire orphan dark-blue vertical bus at the extreme left of the picture (x approximately 20 to 65), together with its three right-pointing arrowheads/short wires entering the LEFT edges of CPU, Vortex SimX, and CoralNPU RTL boxes. Fill erased areas with the same clean white background. The three processor boxes must connect ONLY from their RIGHT edges to the existing shared bus and Native AXI256. Keep all boxes, right-side connections, bidirectional native AXI256 / AXI2Flit / UCIe path, memory-side dispatcher, ordinary-access bypass, online mem_sim, SparseGate RTL blocks, arrows, text, layout, colors, resolution, white background and academic style unchanged. Do not introduce a bottom return wire or a new connection. No other changes.

Edit the attached English academic architecture diagram as a crisp, precise wide 2055×765 white-background technical figure. Preserve its navy/teal thin-line style and downstream topology. On the LEFT, REMOVE the CPU and CoralNPU RTL boxes and every wire from them. Replace the left Vortex SimX box with a single prominent box EXACTLY labeled 'Vortex CP DMA'. It is the ONLY command sender. Draw a bidirectional line from that box to 'Native AXI256', then bidirectional 'AXI2Flit', 'UCIe', and 'Memory-side dispatcher'. From dispatcher, upper bidirectional path labeled 'Ordinary accesses' goes to 'Online mem_sim'; lower path labeled 'Gate MMIO requests / responses' goes into the 'AXI256 registers' inside 'SparseGate RTL'. Preserve dashed SparseGate RTL enclosure containing, left-to-right, 'AXI256 registers', 'FP4 index core', 'Stable Top-K', 'AXI256 DMA', linked in sequence. Keep bidirectional vertical DMA-to-Online mem_sim connection labeled 'Index reads / KV gather / result writes'. Do not show CPU or CoralNPU anywhere. Do not add a second command sender, a bypass around UCIe, or a GPU core. Ensure arrows and all text are clean, legible, accurately spelled. At bottom, write 'Vortex CP DMA sends gate commands through AXI/UCIe' and 'One event timeline; one memory image'. Match the original aspect ratio and publication-quality schematic clarity.
prompts.note: Vortex CP DMA is the only illustrated gate command source; CPU and CoralNPU ordinary sources are omitted.
